text:
maya: Heads up — saw a small spike where a handful of SSE clients suddenly reconnected repeatedly for ~3m. Console shows duplicate token counts for affected routes. Not the usual resume-id dupes, looks like an edge throttle callback returning an empty 204 that the client treats as closed.

kevin: Can you paste the proxy logs? 204 from CDN edge on streaming sounds odd.

maya: Here's the snippet from edge-prod:```
[edge-12] 2026-02-14T09:12:03Z GET /v1/stream 200 keepalive=1
[edge-12] 2026-02-14T09:12:04Z throttle-inflight id=route-42 inflight=120 limit=120 -> action=drain
[edge-12] 2026-02-14T09:12:04Z proxy-resp status=204 content-length=0
```

sophie: Wait, our streaming path expects either chunked data or a clean close (terminal chunk). A 204 is effectively a silent no-op — client lib interprets it as EOF and issues resume/reconnect.

alan: That rings a bell — we have code in the CDN plugin that tries to short-circuit to reduce memory when inflight hits limit; it used to return 429 but someone changed to 204 to avoid long client-side errors.

kevin: Oof. So client reconnects -> resume flow -> server accepts new session while old session still being accounted for in billing window -> double-charge. Console shows both sessions as active for a bit because resume ids didn't match and route affinity swapped.

maya: Repro steps I used: 1) open SSE with keepalive every 15s 2) flood ~125 parallel streams for same tenant 3) force inflight limit on edge 4) observe client sees immediate close and reconnect loop.

alan: Minimal fix: change the plugin to return 429 with Retry-After and a small body explaining throttling. Client should honor 429 and backoff instead of immediate resume.

kevin: Agree. But we should also add a console annotation / metric: mark sessions closed by edge-throttle so billing reconciler can dedupe duplicates during the window. Right now console traces only 'session_open' and 'session_resume' events.

sophie: I'd prefer we add a telemetry field in the streaming headers: X-Resume-Allowed: true/false and X-Edge-Throttle-Reason to tag when the edge actively drained. Then billing job can ignore resumes within 10s of a drain-tagged close.

maya: Nice. For rollout UX: can we gate the change (429 behavior + header) behind a feature flag per-region? We should canary in us-west first.

kevin: Yes. Plan: (a) quick patch to plugin to switch 204 -> 429 + Retry-After=5 (hotfix, rollbackable) (b) instrument header X-Edge-Drain in proxy (c) add console telemetry + reconcile rule in billing (d) canary deploy us-west -> monitor duplicate-charge metric + latency.

alan: I'll open the PR for the proxy change now. Quick ask: maintainers, add an automated test that simulates inflight cap and asserts 429 response body rather than 204, and that keepalive chunks are preserved when the client is not over limit.

deploy-bot: Maya requested a canary rollout tag: canary/edge-throttle-429 on us-west.

kevin: Also, client-side mitigations: suggest we update the JS/Swift SDKs to treat 204 on streaming as a transient 429-equivalent backoff (if encountered) — as defense-in-depth in case some edge still returns 204 from older versions.

sophie: Good call. I'll file a small SDK issue and draft the SDK change.

maya: For telemetry/dashboard: please add a new alert rule: if duplicate-session-ratio > 1.5% for a tenant and attributed to edge-drain, fire P1. We had a confused customer pinging support.

alan: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/proxy/merge/2137 — patch + unit tests. I'll keep it on a short-lived branch for canary.

ops-bot: Alert muted in #oncall for 15m while canary deploy proceeds.

kevin: Postmortem items: track impact (#tokens double-counted), add billing reconciler rule, and improve runbook to check edge plugin versions.

maya: Thanks all. If we see residual dupes after canary, we'll revert plugin and push SDK defences. :thumbsup:
